title: He got more time.
paragraphs:
What if the thing you’re begging God for…
is the very thing that will reveal what you’ve been hiding?

What if answered prayer doesn’t fix you—
it unmasks you?
Because this is where it gets uncomfortable.
We love the part where King Hezekiah cried out and God answered.

We quote it.
We celebrate it.
We claim it.
But we rarely talk about what those extra years exposed.
Hezekiah was humble… until he wasn’t.
And comfort has a way of awakening pride you thought was already buried.
A king who just survived death.
A man who should have been marked by gratitude.
And instead of giving glory to God—

His treasures.
His gold.
His weapons.
His storehouses.
Like a man saying, “Look what I have.”
the crack in his heart became visible.

“Then Hezekiah welcomed them and showed them all his treasure house… there was nothing in his house or in all his realm that Hezekiah did not show them.”
—2 Kings 20:13 (ESV)
Except the one thing that mattered most—
Some scholars interpret this moment as political strategy.
a heart drifting from worship to self-exaltation.
Because this isn’t just Hezekiah’s story.
Now… do you still seek Him like you did in the hospital?
Now… do you still depend on Him—or flex what you have?
Now… is your heart softer—or more self-sufficient?
Here’s the truth we don’t like:
Pride rarely shows up in crisis.

After the breakthrough.
After the blessing.
After the miracle.
Because you can have more time…
Hezekiah’s extra years didn’t automatically produce deeper holiness.
They revealed what was still unhealed.

“Behold, the days are coming, when all that is in your house… shall be carried to Babylon.”
—2 Kings 20:17
Because this is where shame tries to creep in.

“Is that me?”
“Have I drifted?”
“Did I waste what God gave me?”
But don’t stay in condemnation either.
Because this is where the Gospel breaks in.
You are not saved by how well you handled your “extra time.”
You are saved by what Jesus did with His.
Where Hezekiah begged to avoid death—

“He humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death—even death on a cross.”
—Philippians 2:8
Where Hezekiah exposed his treasures to impress men—
Jesus gave up His glory to save sinners.
Where Hezekiah’s pride led to future loss—
You and I have hearts that drift.
But Jesus came not just to give you more time—
He came to give you a new heart.

“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.”
—2 Corinthians 5:17
This means your story doesn’t end in pride.
It doesn’t end in wasted years.
What are you doing with the time God has already given you?
Not the time you wish you had.
Are you using it to glorify Him—
Time to realign your heart with Christ.
Don’t just ask God for more years.
Ask Him for a surrendered heart.
Don’t just ask Him to fix your situation.
Ask Him to transform your soul.
